network.tdh.spec.metadataDescription: The exact written form of the TDH rule, as proposed: every input, formula and rounding step, in readable form.
network.tdh.spec.title: The TDH-v1 specification
network.tdh.spec.lede: TDH-v1 is the exact written form of the TDH rule, proposed as the rule every implementation computes to the last unit. It restates 6529.io’s formula; section 11 lists every place it departs, with the effect measured.
network.tdh.spec.mapDesc: Inputs (section 2) feed canonical events (3), which set the snapshot (4). Eligibility and rates (5) and identities (6) both feed holdings (7), which feed scores (8) and the day’s output (9). The parameter registry (10) feeds sections 2 to 8: contract addresses, sinks, the day length, editions and rates, the consolidation use case and group size, and the boosts.
network.tdh.spec.s1.title: 1. Scope and conventions
network.tdh.spec.s1.body: TDH-v1 defines, for one day, each wallet’s and identity’s balance, whole days, base, boost and final TDH per eligible token, and the network totals; ranks, xTDH, REP and upload files are out of scope. Arithmetic is exact, on integers and fractions. B64, the nearest binary64 number, is applied where the rule writes it, in RATE and FINAL; there it changes the exact half-up result only at an exact tie (sections 8.1 and 8.4). Every number and address comes from the rule version’s registry (section 10).
network.tdh.spec.s2.title: 2. Inputs
network.tdh.spec.s2.body: One day’s inputs are Ethereum’s canonical chain up to the snapshot block, every event of four contracts up to that block, the edition-floor state of a fifth contract read at that block, and the rule version’s parameter list. Prices, Meme Lab, received xTDH, REP and $6529 balances are not inputs.
network.tdh.spec.s2.tableCaption: Four event sources and one state read
network.tdh.spec.s2.delegationEvents: Register and revoke, direct and through a sub-delegate
network.tdh.spec.s2.manifoldEvents: getClaimForToken, read at the snapshot block
network.tdh.spec.s2.topicsCaption: Topic hashes, keccak-256 of each signature
network.tdh.spec.s3.title: 3. Canonical events
network.tdh.spec.s3.body: Every event is read exactly once, decoded strictly, and put in one order that everyone can reproduce: block, then transaction, then log, then position in a batch. A node that cannot show it has every event must not publish, and a malformed event invalidates the day’s input rather than being skipped.
network.tdh.spec.s3.sinks: A mint comes from the zero address to any other address and debits nobody; a transfer from the zero address to itself moves nothing and is not a mint. A transfer to a sink, the zero address or 0x…dead in tdh-v1.0, is a burn. Sinks are credit-only: they receive records but are never debited and never consolidated. The FirstGM burn transaction is not credited to the zero address. Burns do not reduce edition sizes.
network.tdh.spec.s4.title: 4. Day, snapshot and whole days
network.tdh.spec.s4.body: Day N closes at N × 86,400 seconds, 00:00 UTC. Its snapshot block is the last block before that moment on the finalized chain, and ages are measured to that block’s time.
network.tdh.spec.s4.binds: The result binds (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash).
network.tdh.spec.s5.title: 5. Eligibility, editions, rates and seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.title: 5.1 Eligibility
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.body: Memes and Gradients count when their first mint, of any amount, is at least eligibility_min_age_s (86,400 s) before T; a transfer from the zero address to itself is not a mint. NextGen tokens count when minted at or before B. n_memes is the number of eligible Memes, a count.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.title: 5.2 Editions and floors
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.body: A Meme’s edition is the copies minted; burns do not reduce it. Below 300 copies minted it gets a floor, its claim’s totalMax up to 310, and counts at the larger of the two.
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.title: 5.3 Rates
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.body: Meme i: RATE(H, E[i]). Gradient: RATE(H, G), at least the registry’s gradient_rate_minimum (1.00), G = Gradients minted at or before B. NextGen token t: RATE(H, N_c), c = t div 10^10, N_c = tokens of collection c minted at or before B. With no eligible Meme, H = 0: Gradients get the 1.00 minimum and NextGen 0.
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.title: 5.4 Seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.body: Seasons come from the registry’s season_starts, the first Meme id of each season: 1, 48, 87, 119, 152, 181, 213, 246, 279, 311, 343, 375, 407, 439, 477, 516, 556. The list must start at 1 and strictly increase, or the registry is invalid. A season is listed for a day when its first id is at most n_memes; the highest listed is current. Seasons 1 to 20 carry a 0.05 bonus; a season pays when it is not current and its bonus is positive. A new season must be added, as a new rule version, before its first card becomes eligible.
network.tdh.spec.s6.title: 6. Consolidation
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.title: 6.1 Events
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.body: Only delegation events with use case 999, for The Memes or the all-collections address 0x8888…8888, between two different wallets neither of which is a sink, count: a sink is never consolidated. Every event’s position is checked, kept or not; two events at one position make the input invalid. Expiry, allTokens, token id and update events are ignored.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.title: 6.2 Pair state
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.body: Each unordered pair of wallets has at most one row. A registration in one direction is pending; the other direction confirms it. The collection does not partition the state.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.machineDesc: Three states: no row, pending in one direction, and confirmed. REGISTER(a, b) creates a row pending from a to b; REGISTER(b, a) on that row confirms it. REVOKE on a confirmed row returns it to pending in the other direction, as the other wallet’s registration; REVOKE by the registering side of a pending row deletes it.
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.title: 6.3 Identities
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.body: Confirmed pairs, newest first, grow cliques of at most 3 wallets in which every pair is confirmed; a wallet joins at most one.
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.title: 6.4 and 6.5 Effective state and identity key
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.body: The grouping after all events up to B applies to the whole history of the day’s calculation. An identity’s key is its sorted lowercase addresses joined by “-”.
network.tdh.spec.s7.title: 7. Holdings
network.tdh.spec.s7.body: Three steps, in this order: an underflow test over the transfers before netting, transaction netting, and the replay of the netted transfers into each wallet’s acquisition stacks.
network.tdh.spec.s8.title: 8. Arithmetic and scores
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.title: 8.1 Rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.body: RATE equals half-up of 100n/d except at an exact half cent; with H = 3,941 that happens only for editions 8, 40, 56, 200, 280 and 1,400. The Gradient minimum comes from the registry.
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.title: 8.2 Base
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.body: Multiply the rate in cents by the whole days and round half up to a whole TDH. This equals the old backend’s two-step rounding.
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.title: 8.3 Boost
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.body: A record holds a token when the token is eligible and the balance is positive, whatever the copies’ ages. ADD’s first term and ratio come from the registry, and ADD stops growing once it reaches the limit of its rounded values; a program derives that point from the registry and must not hard-code it. For tdh-v1.0: ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 for n ≥ 33. The cent rounding never meets a tie.
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.title: 8.4 Final
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.body: FINAL is computed per token; a record’s final is the sum. Ties round down only for some boosts and some bases, the smallest being base 25 at 1.14.
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.title: 8.5 Totals
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.body: The total is the sum of identity finals, never of wallet finals. A second total leaves out the sink identities, one per registry sink, since a sink is never consolidated; sinks never enter any consensus weight.
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.title: 8.6 Daily rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.body: rate_e4 = beta × the sum of the rates of each copy with at least one whole day, in 10^-4 TDH a day; derived data.
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.title: 8.7 Range
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.body: A day is inside the tdh-v1.0 range when H, G, every N_c, every base × beta and the total are below 2^53, every net movement of section 7.1’s netting is below 2^64 (vector 50), and every balance and raw of a wallet or identity record, per token and in total, is below 2^64 (vector 58). Outside it there is no result. Inside it, hardware binary64 and exact emulation agree, and every output value fits 64 bits.
network.tdh.spec.s9.title: 9. The day’s output
network.tdh.spec.s9.body: The header (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash), and per identity its key, wallets, boost and final, with per-token balance, raw, base and final; the per-token final is what card-set credit uses. Wallet records, daily rates and totals are derived. The encodings (P28) and the signed root (P53) are in 6529’s private design repository; this section restates the cycle root validators are to sign and its two trees, and conformance needs nothing more from them.
network.tdh.spec.s10.title: 10. Parameters
network.tdh.spec.s10.body: Every number the rule uses is a parameter of the rule version, read at its type; programs hard-code none of them. tdh-v1.0 is not frozen until launch, so changes made before it, such as D131’s netting, stay tdh-v1.0; from launch on, any change is a new rule version with its own first cycle.
network.tdh.spec.s10.name: Name
network.tdh.spec.s10.hashNote: Recomputed with the Python reference; conformance vector 28 checks it. TH is P28’s tagged hash of the canonical encodings, defined below; P28 writes it H, and this page writes TH so that H stays the largest edition. The rows marked “formula” are not fields of the record: the rule version string tdh-v1.0 fixes them, so they are not hashed.

network.tdh.spec.param.edition_floor_thr: Floors apply only below this many copies

network.tdh.spec.param.consolidation_use: The delegation use case for consolidation

network.tdh.spec.s11.title: 11. Where TDH-v1 differs from the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s11.body: Nineteen differences from the old backend, each with what it did, what TDH-v1 does, the effect measured and the decision. On the replayed cycle none changes a value. The only one that did, DEV-2, came from tokens sent out and back within one transaction, which D131’s netting removes; DEV-2’s other case, a sale and a purchase in different transactions of one block, changed no value that day and can still differ until the cutover.

network.tdh.spec.s12.title: 12. Issues found in the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s12.body: Fifteen issues found in the old backend, and what TDH-v1 does about each: most are removed; BUG-7’s carry over history and BUG-9 are kept by decision, and BUG-15 concerns upload files, which TDH-v1 does not define.

network.tdh.spec.s13.title: 13. Conformance
network.tdh.spec.s13.body: A program conforms when it reproduces all 89 conformance vectors (01 to 88 and 12b, as of f840096) and, for a real day, the reference implementation’s output from the same inputs; a vector with no result asserts only that there is none. As of October 16, 2026 the Python and Rust references pass all 89, as do the Rust core and program B on the validator’s development branch (30bf8f9). Each day’s page names the builds the daily comparison ran.
network.tdh.spec.decisions.title: Decisions referenced
network.tdh.spec.decisions.intro: The owner’s decisions these pages cite. The decision record is in 6529’s private design repository.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D112: Validator v1 agrees on TDH once a day, peer to peer: each validator computes TDH-v1 with the Rust core, signs the result and compares it with 6529.io.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D116: The validator code is licensed under Apache 2.0. It stays private until the owner publishes it, which is to happen before the first outside operator runs it; publishing it also publishes the ported TDH-v1 core and its conformance vectors.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D118: Every validator checks each block’s events against Ethereum’s block headers, and the headers against a finalized block its own light client follows; a node that cannot complete the checks does not sign.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D119: Two separately written programs, A and B, are to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s own history in two different zero-knowledge virtual machines; both are being built.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D121: One TDH formula everywhere: 6529.io, its backend and the validators compute identical TDH with the validators’ Rust core; the open deviations are settled as listed in section 11.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D125: Every validator computes TDH with two separately written implementations before it signs, and does not sign if they disagree; anyone can add the Python reference as a third.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D128: A minimal Ethereum contract is to record a day’s result once both programs’ proofs verify. It is being built and tested against a fork of Ethereum mainnet; nothing is deployed until the owner approves.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D130: A new validator may take the TDH history from the network’s agreement, or check all of it itself.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D131: Ownership is read at transaction boundaries: within one transaction, each wallet’s movements of each token are netted. P26 §7.1 carries the exact rule.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D132: From October 16, 2026 the Rust core and the Python reference run daily beside 6529.io’s backend and are shown side by side; 6529.io switches to the Rust result about one week later, around October 23, 2026.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.title: Evidence
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.title: Replay of 2026-10-11
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.body: From the live per-token inputs, TDH-v1 reproduces all 132,481 wallet-token bases and every wallet and identity value. From the 388,335 indexed transfers it reproduced 10,278 of 10,280 identities and 11,128 of 11,130 wallets before D131; the two others were tokens sent out and back in one transaction (DEV-2). With D131’s netting it reproduces all 10,280 identities and 11,130 wallets. The validator’s own Ethereum ingestion later read the raw logs from each contract’s deployment, with the history not yet fully checked: on them the Python reference with netting gives 2,061,888,816, the live total, and equals every live identity and wallet, and the second implementation agrees on every record. The input rules written out later, on October 15 and 16, change nothing on that input: its 414,007 logs pass every position and header-order check, every value is in its type, and the transfers of each log share their contract, sender and recipient.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.cleanRoom.body: The Rust reference, written from P26, its vectors, the reference README and the documents P26 cites, without opening the Python reference or the backend’s code, recorded 23 places where it had to choose (2 high, 11 medium, 10 low). P26 now states a rule for every one; the last, the state-read adapter for edition floors (F-10), was pinned in P53 §11.3 on October 16.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.comparison.bod: From independent inputs (Ethereum logs, history not yet fully checked), the Rust core is compared with 6529.io’s published files in every compared field. On the first two days, October 14 and 15, before D131: 10,280 of 10,282 identities and 11,131 of 11,133 wallets equal each day; the two others were tokens sent out and back within one transaction (DEV-2). With D131’s netting: all 10,282 identities and 11,133 wallets, with totals equal to the uploads’ (2,070,436,337 and 2,073,214,934). Ranks, the balance and set-count columns (BUG-15) and display fields are not compared.
network.tdh.spec.symbols.title: Symbols
network.tdh.spec.symbol.M: The cycle’s boundary, N × 86,400 seconds: 00:00 UTC
network.tdh.spec.symbol.B: The snapshot block: on the finalized chain, the block b with ts(b) < M ≤ ts(b + 1) (section 4.2)
network.tdh.spec.symbol.T: The snapshot block’s timestamp; ages are measured to it
network.tdh.spec.symbol.days: Whole days, of the registry’s day_s, from an acquisition time a to T
network.tdh.spec.symbol.H: The largest effective edition among eligible Memes
network.tdh.spec.symbol.G: Gradients minted at or before B
network.tdh.spec.symbol.Nc: NextGen collection c’s tokens minted at or before B
network.tdh.spec.symbol.net: Address w’s net movement of one token in one transaction
network.tdh.spec.symbol.raw: A token’s whole days, summed over its copies
network.tdh.spec.symbol.base: Rate × raw, rounded: a token’s TDH before the boost
network.tdh.spec.symbol.sets: Full sets: the smallest balance of any eligible Meme, when every one is held
network.tdh.spec.symbol.B64: The nearest binary64 number; it decides ties
network.tdh.spec.symbol.SINKS: The registry’s sinks: the zero address and 0x…dead in tdh-v1.0
network.tdh.spec.s3.decoding: The event signatures and their topic hashes are in section 2.
network.tdh.spec.s7.property: The stacks depend only on each transaction’s net movement of each token per address: steps inside a transaction that leave every net movement unchanged change no stack (vectors 45 to 47). The Lean model proves this for two replays whose transactions correspond one to one and in order, starting from transfers already in canonical order; adding or removing a whole transaction is not covered. Balances and raw days follow from the stacks for every token whose eligibility stays the same, by section 7.2’s definitions; that is not a theorem of the model.
network.tdh.spec.decision.legend: All settled by D121; DEV-2 amended by D131. Adopted: TDH-v1’s rule, which changed no value on the replayed cycle. Spec wins: on-chain order across transactions, netting within one. Old behavior kept: TDH-v1 keeps the backend’s behavior. Kept, not in consensus: sink records stay, and never count toward consensus weight.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t1: No row, then REGISTER(a, b): pending, registered by a.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t2: Pending, then the other wallet registers back: confirmed.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t3: Confirmed, then either wallet revokes: pending again, as the other wallet’s registration.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t4: Pending, then the registering wallet revokes: no row.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t5: Confirmed, then the confirming direction registers again: still confirmed, with a newer position.
network.tdh.spec.s7.underflow: Exact rule, step 1: the underflow test, before netting
network.tdh.spec.s7.replay: Exact rule, step 3: the replay, after netting
network.tdh.spec.s3-1.title: 3.1 Log selection and positions
network.tdh.spec.s3-1.body: Every log of the four event contracts up to the snapshot block is an input, exactly once, ignored logs included. A log’s place is its block and log index; the checks below run on the inputs, before delegation events are filtered and before transfers are netted.
network.tdh.spec.s3-2.title: 3.2 Decoding
network.tdh.spec.s3-2.body: Three transfer events yield transfers, each decoded byte for byte from its canonical Solidity encoding. Every value has a type, and a value outside it, or written any other way, makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.s3-3.title: 3.3 Order
network.tdh.spec.s3-3.body: Zero-amount and self transfers move nothing but are kept, because a zero-amount mint is how a card is created. Transfers in different transactions keep on-chain order, even within one block. Within one transaction, each token’s movements are first netted (section 7.1); section 5’s mint facts (each card’s first mint and minted count, G and N_c), the underflow test and the position checks read the transfers before netting.
network.tdh.spec.s3-4.title: 3.4 Mints, burns and sinks
network.tdh.spec.s7-1.title: 7.1 Acquisition stacks
network.tdh.spec.s7-2.title: 7.2 Per-token values
network.tdh.spec.s7-2.body: For each eligible token a wallet holds: its balance is the number of copies, its raw days the sum of each copy’s whole days, and its base the rate times the raw days, rounded. Tokens that are not eligible contribute nothing, not even balance.
network.tdh.spec.s7-3.title: 7.3 Records
network.tdh.spec.s7-3.body: A wallet has a record when it holds an eligible token or belongs to a group; an identity has a record when one of its wallets does. An identity’s balance, raw days and base are the sums of its wallets’, and its base is never recomputed from merged days. Boost and final are computed per record, so an identity’s final is not the sum of its wallets’ finals: two wallets that each hold one Gradient with base 100 have finals 102 and 102, and their identity, holding two Gradients, 208.
network.tdh.spec.s7.limit: The property stops there. Three things read the transfers before netting: section 5’s mint facts, the underflow test (vector 44) and section 3.1’s position checks. So a mint and its burn inside one transaction change no stack, but can make a token eligible and change editions, rates and seasons, and through eligibility balances, raw days and other holders’ TDH. In the Lean model’s counterexample I a wallet with no record gets a balance of 5 and another holder’s final goes from 32 to 60; in counterexample H another holder’s final doubles, from 800 to 1,600.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.difftest.title: Four-way differential tests, October 15 and 16, 2026
network.tdh.spec.evidence.difftest.body: Generated cycles ran through the Lean model, the Python reference, the Rust core and program B in five rounds. Each round’s findings became rules in P26, pinned by new vectors. In the fifth round, on October 16, all four agreed on all 30,000 main cases; its edge probes found one open question for the vector format (E13).
network.tdh.spec.symbol.registry: The parameter list of the rule version, with its hash

network.tdh.spec.implementers.title: For implementers
network.tdh.spec.implementers.body: Everything needed to conform is on this page: the values and records of sections 4 to 8, the output of section 9 and the registry hash of section 10. The vectors check those, and no vector checks a root. Section 9 also restates the cycle root validators are to sign, with its two trees. The rest of P28, such as the history root and the signature domains, is not needed to conform and is only in the private document. Today an implementation can be checked against the registry hash (vector 28) and vector 36, restated in full on the implementations page; the other vectors come with their publication (D116).
network.tdh.spec.changes.title: Changes since October 15
network.tdh.spec.changes.intro: P26 changed six times on October 15, 2026, and once on October 16. Two changes concern a real day’s values: the edition-floor correction and D131’s netting.
network.tdh.spec.changes.floors: Edition floors limited to Memes below 300 copies (section 5.2): a correction, caught before launch, of a text that as written would have raised Memes 206, 215 and 311 to a 310-copy floor and lowered 285 identities by 111,494 TDH on the October 11 cycle.
network.tdh.spec.changes.netting: Transaction netting (D131) entered section 7.1, then was made uniform; it brought the two DEV-2 identities of October 11 back to 6529.io’s values.
network.tdh.spec.changes.inputs: Four rounds wrote out the input rules that the Lean model, the four-way differential tests and their reviews asked about: log positions, logs given raw or decoded, and transfers at one log position sharing contract, sender and recipient (3.1); value types and how values are written in JSON (3.2, 10); cycle dates and the cutoff block in the header set (4.1, 4.2); ZERO to ZERO is not a mint (3.4); the claim limit’s type (5.2); a sink is never consolidated (6.1); the bound on balances (8.7); and a registry that programs read in full, with its constraints (10).
network.tdh.spec.changes.vectors: The conformance vectors grew from 35 to 89. The other changes leave every value of the October 11 cycle as it was.
network.tdh.spec.s9.root: Validators are to sign one hash, the cycle root (P53 §4.2): the day, its snapshot block, the rule version with its registry hash, the wallet tree, the per-token tree, and the counts and total. Two validators agree on a day when their cycle roots are equal.

network.tdh.spec.s10.hashRuleTitle: Exact rule: how H and the record are encoded
network.tdh.spec.s11.pending: 6529.io accepts four consolidated wallets since October 15, 2026, while tdh-v1.0 groups at most three. Which applies is pending an owner decision.
network.tdh.spec.s9.leavesTitle: Exact rule: the wallet and per-token trees
network.tdh.spec.s9.leaves: Both trees pair adjacent entries left to right, promote an odd last entry unchanged and bind their leaf count into the root (P28 §3.3, §4.3, §4.4 and §4.12).
network.tdh.spec.s10.formulaTitle: Not a field of the registry record: fixed by the rule version tdh-v1.0, and not hashed
network.tdh.spec.s7.replayNote: Removal is from the end of the sending wallet’s list. After a move inside an identity an old timestamp can be last, and it is then removed first: this is the old backend’s behaviour, and P26 says it MUST be kept.
network.tdh.spec.symbol.Hhash: P28’s tagged hash, the keccak256 of abi.encode(TAG(name), …), used for the registry hash and the roots; P28 writes it H
network.tdh.spec.versionRow.title: Version
network.tdh.spec.versionRow.ruleValue: tdh-v1.0, not frozen until launch: changes made before launch stay tdh-v1.0 (section 10)
network.tdh.spec.versionRow.textValue: Specification P26 at commit f840096, its latest change, October 16, 2026
network.tdh.spec.versionRow.whereValue: P26, its vectors and the Lean model are in 6529’s private design repository. The validator source, which carries a copy of the vectors, is to be published when the owner decides; no date is set.
network.tdh.spec.versionRow.statusValue: A proposal, not yet adopted as a consensus rule. By the owner’s decisions 6529.io computes it from the cutover, about October 23, 2026, and every validator once validators run.

network.tdh.spec.decision.D120: Anyone can set up and run a validator with nothing run by 6529: the code is open source (D116) with reproducible builds, and the comparison with 6529.io is optional.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.day: N counts the days since January 1, 1970. A date names a day only when it is exactly eight digits of a real calendar date on or after that day.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.result: The day has no result until the block after the snapshot block is finalized too.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.ages: Ages are whole days of the registry’s day_s, 86,400 seconds.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.order: Header timestamps must strictly increase over every header a node reads for the day, adjacent or not; a decoded transfer stamped after T, in a block at or before B, makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.example: Example: the upload dated 2026-10-11 is day 20,737, boundary 1,791,676,800.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.detail.why310: The floor stands for copies still to come: below 300 copies, a final airdrop brings an edition to 310, above The Memes’ 300-copy minimum (the Nakamoto Threshold). An older claim of 300 gives 300.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.detail.noFloor: From 300 copies on there is no floor, and a Meme with no claim has none.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.detail.totalMax: totalMax is a 32-bit number, read at the snapshot block through an adapter that P53 §11.3 pins.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.detail.zero: A Meme with an effective edition of 0 is eligible but has no rate, and a copy of it in any stack makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.heroFacts: Not public yet: P26, its vectors and the Lean model are in 6529’s private design repository, and the vectors are to be published with the validator code (D116). Testable today: the registry hash (vector 28) and vector 36, restated in full on the implementations page.
